themes.label: Multi-stakeholder partnerships incl. GPAI
themes.definition: AI appears via international partnership initiatives (e.g. Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence) championed as part of a new governance of the digital common good.
themes.inclusion: Include references to international AI partnerships or coalitions as governance instruments.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic digital governance with no AI reference (DIGITAL_PUBLIC_ORDER_ONLINE).
themes.boundary_cases: When AI is only named as one partnership among digital initiatives, code here with low salience and also the digital theme.

examples.quote: the International Partnership on Information and Democracy of the Christchurch Appeal and the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence

themes.label: Digital commons governance against hate, terrorism
themes.definition: Generic digital-space governance: treating the internet as a common good and regulating platforms against terrorism and hate speech; not AI-specific.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on internet public order, platform accountability, online terrorism and hate speech regulation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages specifically about AI systems or AI-generated content (e.g. AI_DISINFORMATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Platform regulation mentioned alongside an AI partnership is coded here for the platform content and under AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE for the AI reference.

examples.quote: requires a new type of governance so that it is not captured, pirated and exploited
the creation of a common public order on the Internet are as important as technological innovation and freedom

value.rationale: France 2020 discusses governance of the digital space broadly (hate, terrorism, platforms); AI appears only through naming the Global Partnership on AI, so the AI mention is peripheral to a generic digital-governance argument.
